source.title: Dynamical similarity analysis can identify compositional dynamics developing in RNNs
source.authors: Quentin Guilhot; Michał Wójcik; Jascha Achterberg; Rui Ponte Costa

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or wrong-document issue; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares representational-similarity measures and measures how representation similarity varies with training-schedule overlap, but does not test convergence with model scale or cross-modal convergence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports direct similarity measurements on simulated attractors, trained RNNs, and Mamba models. Cited findings from Driscoll et al. are background, not cataloged as this study's results. Hyperparameter selection values are not recorded as result rows.
record.test_reason: A benchmark of dynamical similarity metrics on trained RNNs and Mamba models. Its results show that conclusions about whether independently trained networks have similar representations depend on the metric: DSA separates training schedules, while CKA and Procrustes do not (RNNs) or reach the opposite conclusion (Mamba). That bears on V6. The shared-task overlap regression gives weak, indirect evidence on the shared-training part of V7. Nothing here tests scale, cross-modal, seed, mapping or feature-universality versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that DSA is the strongest of the three metrics. It is slightly more noise-robust on attractors, and it is the only one that recovers the expected compositional ordering in RNNs and links representation to accuracy; CKA and Procrustes fail on the RNN test case. They add that RNN representations develop in discrete groups (none, partial, full pretraining), not gradually. They also say DSA suggests Mamba learns these tasks in a reservoir-like way. They frame all of this as exploratory and not a full validation of DSA.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares DSA, CKA, and Procrustes on simulated dynamical systems and trained recurrent/state-space models; it does not reproduce a cross-model convergence-with-scale method.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity outcomes depend on metric: DSA, CKA, and Procrustes differ in noise response and in whether they distinguish RNN training schedules. DSA hyperparameters were selected using attractor analyses; the authors state that changing them affected results quantitatively but not qualitatively.

fits_no_version.finding: DSA dissimilarity rises with the accuracy gap between networks (slope 0.22, R²=0.13), while CKA and Procrustes show small negative slopes (R²≈0.01).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Only some similarity metrics link representational similarity to behavioural (task-accuracy) similarity in RNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Metric differences on simulated noisy and composed Lorenz attractors are small. DSA is slightly more noise-robust, and all metrics respond near-linearly to composition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On synthetic attractor dynamics, DSA, CKA and Procrustes behave similarly, with DSA slightly more noise-robust.

record.problems: The paper calls the analyses exploratory and says its two test cases do not fully validate DSA. The RNN behavior comparison uses accuracy as a broad measure, no empirical data are used, and the authors do not establish why CKA and Procrustes perform worse. The study tests a narrow task and architecture setting, not large-scale or cross-modal model convergence.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported similarity results were excluded. Attractor motif identification results are not separately tabulated as rows because they are auxiliary metric-validation results and do not add a distinct result beyond the reported noise and composition tests.

untested.parts: No sweep over scale or capability, and no models with different architectures, objectives or data compared for convergence.
Networks differ by hyperparameters and training schedule. Comparisons are within matched hyperparameters, but there is no seed-only replication test of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative representations or unpaired alignment.
No interpretable features or circuits compared across models.
No variation of neighbour settings and no out-of-distribution inputs. DSA hyperparameter sensitivity is only asserted ('quantitatively but not qualitatively'), with no data shown.
Does not test whether alignment is far from complete or plateaus. Does not contrast shared training with a common model of reality. Only same-task, small RNNs are used.

missing.what: CKA and Procrustes trajectories by pretraining rank over training. The text says these metrics do not react to the signal DSA shows, which is a metric-dependence result paired with R16.
All-groups-vs-all-groups dissimilarity matrix. DSA keeps the expected ordering with Full Pretraining as reference (0.271, 0.341, 0.600); CKA and Procrustes do not separate the groups.
Per-subtype RNN group tests. For Leaky RNNs, DSA Partial Pretraining is not significant (p=0.22), while some CKA and Procrustes values are lower. This qualifies the metric contrast by architecture.
Mamba comparisons against the Untrained reference. Under DSA, Full Pretraining p=0.75 and Full & Unfrozen p=0.53; under CKA and Procrustes, p≈1e-26 to 1e-29.

record.verdict_notes: This is a metric-benchmark paper whose ground truth comes from Driscoll et al. It is not designed as a convergence study, so its bearing on V6 and V7 is indirect but real: measured similarity between trained networks flips with the metric in the RNN and Mamba analyses. The text says 'DSA and CKA do not identify meaningful differences'. This is evidently a typo for CKA and Procrustes, given Table 5. Mamba models are tiny (hidden size 8–16), and the RNNs are small single-task-family networks.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep testing whether independently trained models become more aligned as they scale.
No paired image-caption or vision-language comparison.
The study does not test whether same-architecture networks trained from different initializations learn shared features or subspaces.
No representation mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits.
It compares DSA, CKA, and Procrustes in selected attractor, RNN, and Mamba analyses. It does not systematically vary nearest-neighbour settings or test out-of-distribution inputs.

It compares representation similarity across task-training schedules and degrees of task overlap. It does not test whether similarity is far from complete, compare independent datasets or objectives, or distinguish shared training causes from a common model of reality.

relation.reason: The study directly compares similarity conclusions across metrics and manipulates training schedules while measuring representational dissimilarity.

tranche.reason: The metric comparisons provide direct results requiring representational-similarity conclusions to be qualified by measurement choice, bearing on V6.

source_check.notes: Row checks cover the content visible in the pack; ellipsized numerical tails cannot be independently audited. Section 4.2 mistakenly names DSA and CKA as failing; its surrounding conclusions, Table 5 and Appendix 6.3 identify CKA and Procrustes.

statements.correction: All three overlap slopes are negative and significant. DSA: slope −0.0048, R² 0.52; CKA: slope −0.0035, R² 0.30; Procrustes: slope −0.0035, R² 0.40. Qualitative direction is robust; quantitative metric independence is not established.
statements.problem: The RNN facts are correct, but the challenges label overstates agreement in direction: regression slopes and explanatory strength still differ across metrics.

statements.correction: Section 4.4 reports distinctions between no, partial and full overlap, without gradual distinctions among partial-overlap schedules. V7 does not specify a graded relationship.
statements.problem: The absence of graded RNN reductions is correctly reported, but treating it as a limitation of V7 adds a graded-response prediction absent from that version.
